passage: Their teacher in Rotterdam had given the class three weeks to build a working model of a wind turbine. Zeynep wrote four words on the whiteboard: Research, Materials, Construction, Presentation. Ingrid loved reading, so she took research. Jamal, who sawed straight and knew it, took construction. Pieter, the talkative one, took presentation. Zeynep kept materials and the calendar for herself. Next to each name went a date: summary by day five, materials by day eight, building from day nine to fifteen, rehearsal on day eighteen. "Everyone has one thing, and a date," she said. On day five Ingrid's summary was on the wall, and Jamal had already sanded his pieces of wood.

qa.a: The class had to build a working model of a wind turbine.

qa.q: What did Zeynep want from giving each person one task and one date?
qa.a: Zeynep wanted everyone to know what was expected of them, and she seemed confident that one task and one date each would stop the work depending on guesses.

qa.q: What could Zeynep do if someone falls behind on a date, and why?
qa.a: Zeynep could check in halfway to the date and offer to swap a small piece of work, because an early conversation is easier than a late rescue.

qa.q: How might Jamal see the task of construction?
qa.a: Jamal likely feels pleased and confident, since it matches what Jamal does best.

passage:
The science lab after school was the only place with enough table space, so the four of them spread out there, surrounded by pipettes they weren't allowed to touch.

Lalremsiami stood at the whiteboard. "Model of a rainwater harvesting system. Due in four weeks. Let's split it properly this time." She wrote four headings: Research, Materials, Building, Presentation.

"Neelam, you're the best at reading papers. Research, done by the 10th." Neelam nodded.

"Aman, your dad's shop has pipes and tape. Materials by the 14th." 

"Pooja, you're good with your hands. Building, the 14th to the 24th."

"And I'll do the presentation, and help Pooja build."

The lab assistant came in to lock up. Lalremsiami snapped a photo of the whiteboard and sent it to the group chat. "Dates are real. If anyone's slipping, say so early."

qa.a: They met in the science lab after school.

qa.q: How might Neelam have felt when Lalremsiami gave Neelam the research?
qa.a: Neelam was likely pleased and trusted, since the task was matched to being the best at reading papers.

qa.q: What else could Lalremsiami add to keep the plan on track?
qa.a: She could set one short weekly check-in, so a slipping date shows up before the building stage is squeezed.

qa.q: How might Pooja see this way of splitting the work?
qa.a: Pooja may feel valued and less anxious, because the building task fits her skills and she has help and clear dates.

grounding: Shows a team leader listing research, materials, building and presentation, giving each member a task that fits their strengths with a date for each stage.

passage:
Dear Simran,

Remember how our Class 8 volcano project was a disaster because everyone did "a bit of everything"? This year I tried something else, and I wanted to tell you.

Our team of four is building a model of a wind turbine for the science fair. On day one I wrote the stages on the back of my notebook: research, materials, construction, presentation. Then I asked each person what they're good at. Anjali loves reading, so she has research until 5 October. Karan's uncle has a hardware shop, so materials by 12 October. Tanmay built a go-kart last summer, so construction until 25 October. I'm doing the presentation.

It's been two weeks, and for once nobody is waiting for somebody else. Karan even brought the motor early.

Wish me luck at the fair!
Lalit

qa.q: By what date was Anjali to finish research?
How is Lalit feeling about the project after two weeks?
qa.a: Lalit feels relieved and hopeful, because for once nobody is waiting for somebody else.

qa.q: What could Lalit add before construction starts?
qa.a: Lalit could check that the materials match what Tanmay needs, so construction does not stall on a missing part.

qa.q: How might Karan see the plan that put him in charge of materials?
qa.a: Karan probably feels useful and trusted, since his uncle's shop made him a natural fit, which may be why he brought the motor early.

grounding: A letter describes a team leader listing project stages, matching each member to a task by strength and setting dates for each stage.
